text:
Mira: Heads up — product is enabling adaptive streaming for the new Assist flow next week. Expect a shift: longer average contexts (proj 1k -> ~3.5–4k tokens), and a bigger streaming fraction (from ~18% -> ~55%). We need a short capacity plan + cost hedge.

Dan: Can you share the expected qps or payload mix? region split? this determines prewarm strategy.

Mira: Rough numbers from Product: global qps up 1.4x during first 72h morning ramp, APAC strong in hour windows (30% of global). Traffic will be 60% streaming by requests, 40% non-streaming. Tail seq distribution: 20% requests > 6k tokens (very small but high impact).

Praveen: Quick calc: if avg stream length -> 3.8k tokens and we keep current batch config, token/s per GPU drops ~2.6x. Short form estimate: baseline GPU-hours/day * 2.1 to 2.7 depending on KV cache hit. Need to choose between more nodes or higher batching latency.

Praveen: Also: streaming increases KV cache pressure and memory residency. We should test warm-pool sizes: n_warm_per_region = 12 -> maybe bump to 28 for APAC/NA preheat window.

Dan: I can prototype a warm-pool rotation. If we preheat extras only for a 6h ramp window we can save steady-state cost. Proposal: add a transient pool with node_ttl=8h and prewarm concurrency tuned.

Dan: snippet of the autoscale tweak I had in mind:
```
PATCH /autoscaler/config
- warm_pool: {size: 12}
+ warm_pool: {size: 12, transient: {extra: 16, ttl: 28800}}
```

Olivia: Finance: ballpark cost delta? if GPU-hours/day *2 => what does that mean for committed vs on-demand mix? Also need to know reserved capacity implications for customers on Dedicated.

Praveen: Ballpark: extra incremental cost for 72h ramp ~ 35–50 GPU-hours per region for our small fleet, bigger if tail >6k. If we shift replica types to q8_128 quantized variants we recover ~20% compute, but regen quality risk for some prompts.

Kai: Oncall constraints: APAC region has lower spare capacity this week (tickets from GCP quota). We should avoid big preheats there unless we have quota confirmed. Also network egress/peering for long contexts has caused intermittent packet drops before — recommend stress test on k8s node egress for 8k payloads.

Mira: Good call. Actionables: 1) Dan -> change warm-pool transient config and test in staging (owner: Dan) 2) Praveen -> run KV + memory pressure sim + provide GPU-hour estimate by EOD (owner: Praveen) 3) Kai -> confirm APAC quota and run egress stress (owner: Kai) 4) Olivia -> fast cost delta with committed vs spot options (owner: Olivia).

Dan: I'll schedule a 1h run tomorrow STAGE with synthetic mix: 55% streaming, 20% >6k. Will post logs and simple perf table.

Praveen: Quick perf targets to track during run: p50 token/s, p99 tail latency (ms per token), GPU util, KV hit %, memory spill events. If p99 token latency > 40ms we need alternative routing to smaller non-stream endpoints.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: assist-adaptive-streaming -> canary start 1965132000, canary window 2h, traffic 5% -> 20%.

Kai: If canary goes green we can autoscale transient pool only for the 2h heavy window instead of 6h. saves cost.

Olivia: If we use transient nodes on-demand for that window, cost delta estimate: +~18% monthly vs baseline if usage spikes repeat weekly; +~4% if it's a one-off launch. Need final GPU-hour numbers to firm this up.

Mira: Also think about fallback policy: route long-stream requests to a slow-path model (higher-latency but cheaper) when util > 85% to preserve success rate. We should add that to rollout checklist.

Dan: noted — I'll wire a routing policy and canary flag: 
```
if util(region) > 0.85 -> route(long_stream) -> model:assist-slowpath-v1
else -> model:assist-fast-v2
```

sre-bot: FYI: last week we saw a node OOM on 8k test payloads in prod-2 cluster; patch 0.12.3 reduced freq but didn't eliminate. Recommend node-level memory margin for long contexts.

Praveen: Ok we'll add 12% memory headroom to the runtime config and validate.

Mira: Thanks all — please post numbers and links to run dashboards in this thread. I'll coordinate with Product for a phased rollout. :rocket: 

Dan: will update with the staging run link and brief table.

Praveen: uploading rough GPU-hour calc now -> https://redwood-internal/infra/runs/1965123460 (staging-sim-results).

Kai: APAC quota confirmed for 24–30 window but not for sustained +50% preheat. We have approval for transient nodes for canary only.

Olivia: noted, preparing short memo for Finance + PM on committed vs transient tradeoffs.

Mira: perfect. closing loop after run.
